title: Automobile
text:
Automobile

A cantata of horns.

Glowworm down the shadowed street.

Shining eyes beneath the cold night.

City reptile sliding swiftly by.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Méndez's urban-machine imagery: horn music, glowworm, eyes, and reptile.

title: Alameda
text:
Alameda:

keep safe

my first seven years.


And the seven

that followed.


And the luminous carousel

of my first loves.


Alameda;

for one day I will return

to gather the finest

or dreams? of my childhood.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Alameda as a remembered place holding childhood, first loves, and uncertain dreams.

title: The Fisherwoman
text:
I do not want the curved pipe,

nor your embroidered handkerchief,

nor the roses on Sundays,

nor the little basket with fish.


And I will leave this port

for another distant port

so that you cannot say:

The fisherwoman is my lover!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the fisherwoman's refusal as a clean escape from being claimed.

title: Ghosts of Ice and Shadow
text:
Ghosts of ice and shadow,

animated and soulless,

surround me everywhere,

wherever I may go.


They surround me and pursue me,

but they never make me cower,

because against the ice they set before me,

I set fire or flame.


With them I am in mourning,

in mourning that does not end.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the duel between ice-shadow ghosts and the speaker's answering flame.

title: Madrigal
text:
Come to me, for you come wounded,

for on this bed of dreams

you can rest with me.


Come, for it is already midnight,

and there is no clock of oblivion

to pour its chimes

into my aching breast.


I was waiting for your return.

From an angle of my life

a voiceless voice announced it to me.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the madrigal as a nocturnal invitation to a wounded beloved.
